Inference-mode dispatch is in [#7579](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7579), FP32 kernels in [#7600](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7600), residual replay in [#6805](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/6805), MTP/MIMO precision in [#6855](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/6855), and modality bridge precision in [#7480](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7480). | ## - [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR. # What does this PR do? Makes the streamwise wide-residual connections from #7599 and HybridStack integration from #6716 compose with Megatron-LM's ShortcutMoE execution introduced by #6959. It uses the FP32 support from #7600, selective replay from #6805, and MTP/MIMO integration from #6855. A ShortcutMoE block groups two physical layers: a supported compute predecessor (attention, Mamba, or Gated DeltaNet) and the following MoE layer. This PR keeps that pair's existing serial or communication-overlapped schedule, while giving each logical consumer the correct ordinary-width read from the carried wide residual stream. It also keeps the physical pair atomic during selective residual-stream replay. > This is the last PR of the wide-residual series. Its prerequisites, including #6855, have merged. ## Issue tracking Linked issue: Related to #6716 ## Algorithm description ```mermaid flowchart TB X["Pair input X_l
[S, B, K, D]"] X --> AR["Compute read c_compute
K*D -> D"] X --> RR["Shortcut routed read c_route
K*D -> D"] AR --> A["Attention / Mamba / GDN
at width D"] A --> AW["Compute carry + write
X_l+1/2 [S, B, K, D]"] RR --> R["Shortcut norm + router
A2A dispatch + routed experts"] AW --> MR["MoE read c_moe
K*D -> D"] MR --> S["MoE norm + shared experts
at width D"] R --> J["Combine routed + shared outputs
optional shortcut post-norm"] S --> J AW -. "carried stream" .-> MW["MoE carry + write"] J --> MW MW --> Y["Pair output X_l+1
[S, B, K, D]"] ``` ## Design ### Independent routed-path read `StreamwiseSigmoidWideResidualRead` is a read-only child module that maps `K * D` to `D` with the same streamwise-sigmoid controller and optimized read operation used by the full residual connection. `ShortcutMoEBlock` owns one such module for the routed shortcut path. The already constructed wide compute and MoE layers continue to own their ordinary branch connections through the architecture-specific classes introduced by the earlier PRs. The block validates that both physical layers agree on MTP and wide-stream participation and that all three consumers agree on the carried width. This keeps model construction explicit: the ShortcutMoE block does not rewrite `ModuleSpec`s or replace layer classes after construction. It only owns the additional read required by the ShortcutMoE dataflow. All parameterized reads are invoked through `apply_module`, so normal module pre-hooks run before controller parameters are accessed. ### Atomic selective replay Residual-stream replay operates on physical layers, whereas `ShortcutMoEBlock` presents a compute/MoE pair as one grouped runtime module. Ending a replay block after the first physical layer would discard or reconstruct state while the shortcut path still depends on the pair input. `build_residual_stream_recompute_plan` therefore accepts adjacent `atomic_layer_pairs`. `HybridStack` reports registered ShortcutMoE pairs and gives the two physical layers separate contexts backed by the same replay manager. The planner packs whole layers or pairs in forward order, closing the current block before a pair that would exceed the target size. It never splits a pair. Runtime validation also requires: - both physical layers to receive replay contexts together; - both contexts to share one manager; and - the compute half not to be a replay-block endpoint. Within the pair: - the routed read and shortcut pre-MLP norm join the predecessor layer's replay context; - the compute read, branch norm, and write use that same first context; - the MoE read, pre-MLP norm, optional shortcut post-norm, and write use the second context; and - block finalization runs after the complete pair returns, and only when the MoE context is a replay-block endpoint. When residual replay owns one of these tensors, fine-grained activation offloading is prevented from also owning it. Other ShortcutMoE offload behavior remains unchanged. ### Transformer, Mamba, MTP, and HybridStack plumbing The two-stage Transformer entry points forward the call-local residual replay context. Mamba shares its one-stage and two-stage schedules through residual-state and update hooks. `WideResidualMambaLayer` owns the wide read/write and replay policy, including explicit post-core dispatch; ordinary `MambaLayer` retains its ordinary normalization and bias-dropout-add helpers. `HybridStack` retains physical layer indices after grouping layers into ShortcutMoE blocks and uses those indices to select the two replay contexts and CP-layout transitions belonging to the pair. MTP auxiliary stacks remain ordinary-width as established by #6855. A ShortcutMoE pair validates that both physical layers agree on MTP status and does not construct a wide routed read inside an MTP auxiliary stack. ## Configuration This PR adds no new CLI or configuration fields. It allows the existing wide-residual and ShortcutMoE options to compose: ```text --wide-residual 3 --moe-shortcut-connection ``` The existing communication-overlap schedule remains optional: ```text --moe-shortcut-parallel ``` Selective wide-residual replay from #6805 also remains optional: ```text --recompute-granularity selective --recompute-modules residual_stream --residual-stream-recompute-num-layers 4 ``` The replay block size is a target physical-layer count. For example, size 3 with pairs `(0, 1)` and `(2, 3)` produces blocks `[0, 1]` and `[2, 3]`. Size 1 still keeps each two-layer pair intact. ## Scope and guardrails - Ordinary ShortcutMoE and non-shortcut wide-residual execution retain their existing paths. - The branch computations, router, routed/shared experts, and collective implementations remain ordinary width `D`. - No Triton or CUDA kernel is added or modified; the new read-only module reuses the streamwise read operation from #7579. - Existing ShortcutMoE restrictions, including inference, CUDA-graph, and FSDP guardrails, remain in force. - This PR does not add a separate pathwise-MoE wide-residual architecture. ## Validation Distributed unit tests compare outputs, input gradients, and finalized parameter gradients at fixed weights: - attention+MoE and Mamba+MoE with real EP=2 All-to-All, serial/overlapped scheduling, and eager/replay execution; - BF16 and FP32 residuals with TP and CP coverage; and - GTP/EGTP=1 versus 2 with FP32 residuals. These are forward/backward parity checks, not optimizer-step training comparisons. ## File guide - `megatron/core/transformer/wide_residual_layer.py`: read-only streamwise routed-path module. - `megatron/core/models/hybrid/shortcut_block.py`: wide routed read, serial/parallel execution, and replay/offload ownership inside a ShortcutMoE pair. - `megatron/core/models/hybrid/hybrid_block.py`: physical-layer context routing and atomic-pair discovery after ShortcutMoE grouping. - `megatron/core/transformer/residual_recompute.py`: atomic replay-plan boundaries. - `megatron/core/transformer/transformer_layer.py`: replay context through two-stage attention. - `megatron/core/ssm/mamba_layer.py`: shared forward schedules and residual-state/update hooks; ordinary helpers remain unchanged. - `megatron/core/ssm/wide_residual_mamba_layer.py`: wide read/write and replay policy, with explicit post-core dispatch. - `megatron/core/transformer/transformer_config.py`: removes the former wide+ShortcutMoE incompatibility guard. - `docs/user-guide/features/fine_grained_activation_offloading.md`: documents replay ownership of ShortcutMoE post-norm activations. - `tests/unit_tests/...`: construction, atomic replay planning, scheduling, and distributed forward/backward parity across EP, TP, CP, and GTP/EGTP. ## Contribution process ### Code review Feel free to message or comment @NVIDIA/mcore-oncall to help accelerate your merge into main. The less complex your PR is, the faster it will be approved and merged! All PRs start as **draft**. If you open a non-draft PR, it will be automatically converted to draft. #### Step 1: Mark PR as "Ready for Review" 1. When your PR is ready, click **Ready for Review**. 2. For PRs outside `megatron/core`, this step is skipped. #### Step 3: Approved Once all required reviewers have approved, the `Approved` label is applied **automatically**. ### Merge Any member of [mcore-engineers](https://github.com/orgs/NVIDIA/teams/mcore-engineers) will be able to merge your PR.

+        wide_residual=WideResidualConfig(num_streams=_STREAMS, learned_retention=True),
+    )
+    if gtp_size > 1:
+        from megatron.core.tensor_parallel.gtp_api import configure_gtp_remat_from_recipe
+
+        configure_gtp_remat_from_recipe()
+    model = (
+        HybridStack(
+            config=config,
+            submodules=wide_residual_hybrid_stack_spec.submodules,
+            layer_config_list=validate_segment_layers(compute_symbol + Symbols.MOE, config),
+            pre_process=not wide_input,
+            post_layer_norm=False,
+            pg_collection=pg_collection,
+        )
+        .cuda()
+        .to(dtype=config.params_dtype)
+    )
+    assert model._residual_stream_atomic_layer_pairs == ((0, 1),)
+    if cp_size > 1:
+        assert model._cp_layout_manager is not None
+    return model
+
+
+def _load_weights(module, saved, pg_collection):
+    assert saved.keys() == dict(module.named_parameters()).keys()
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        for name, parameter in module.named_parameters():
+            value = saved[name]
+            if _is_gtp_parameter(parameter):
+                from megatron.core.tensor_parallel.generalized_tensor_parallelism import (
+                    gtp_remat_slice_rows,
+                )
+
+                group = _weight_group(parameter, pg_collection)
+                value = gtp_remat_slice_rows(value, group)
+            assert value.shape == parameter.shape, name
+            parameter.copy_(value)
+
+
+def _synchronize_weights(module, pg_collection):
+    """Replicate weights within their owner groups, without equating different experts."""
+
+    for parameter in module.parameters():
+        group = (
+            pg_collection.dp_cp_gtp_remat
+            if getattr(parameter, "allreduce", True)
+            else pg_collection.expt_dp_gtp_remat
+        )
+        dist.broadcast(parameter.data, src=dist.get_process_group_ranks(group)[0], group=group)
+
+
+def _local_batch(pg_collection, batch_index, *, sequence_parallel, wide_input):
+    """Different DP/GTP samples; identical samples across a sample's TP/CP peers."""
+
+    generator = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(
+        456 + batch_index * 100 + pg_collection.dp_gtp_remat.rank()
+    )
+    hidden = torch.randn(
+        _SEQUENCE,
+        _BATCH,
+        _HIDDEN * (_STREAMS if wide_input else 1),
+        dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        device="cuda",
+        generator=generator,
+    )
+    target = torch.randn(
+        _SEQUENCE, _BATCH, _HIDDEN, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda", generator=generator
+    )
+    hidden = hidden.chunk(pg_collection.cp.size(), dim=0)[pg_collection.cp.rank()]
+    target = target.chunk(pg_collection.cp.size(), dim=0)[pg_collection.cp.rank()]
+    if sequence_parallel:
+        hidden = hidden.chunk(pg_collection.tp.size(), dim=0)[pg_collection.tp.rank()]
+        target = target.chunk(pg_collection.tp.size(), dim=0)[pg_collection.tp.rank()]
+    return hidden.contiguous().requires_grad_(True), target.contiguous()
+
+
+def _run_forward_backward(module, pg_collection):
+    """Compare two distinct batches at fixed weights through real DDP finalization."""
+
+    module.train()
+    ddp = DistributedDataParallel(
+        module.config,
+        DistributedDataParallelConfig(
+            grad_reduce_in_fp32=True, overlap_grad_reduce=False, use_distributed_optimizer=False
+        ),
+        module,
+        pg_collection=pg_collection,
+    )
+    if pg_collection.gtp_remat.size() > 1 or pg_collection.expt_gtp_remat.size() > 1:
+        from megatron.core.tensor_parallel.gtp_api import classify_gtp_remat_chains
+
+        classify_gtp_remat_chains(ddp)
+    records = []
+    write_dtypes = []
+    read_count = 0
+
+    def record_write(_module, _args, kwargs, output):
+        if kwargs.get("operation") == "write":
+            write_dtypes.append(output.dtype)
+
+    def record_shortcut_read(_module, _args, _output):
+        nonlocal read_count
+        read_count += 1
+
+    pair = module.layers[0]
+    write_handle = pair.moe_layer.residual_connection_mlp.register_forward_hook(
+        record_write, with_kwargs=True
+    )
+    read_handle = pair.shortcut_residual_read.register_forward_hook(record_shortcut_read)
+    try:
+        for batch_index in range(2):
+            reads_before = read_count
+            ddp.zero_grad_buffer()
+            hidden, target = _local_batch(
+                pg_collection,
+                batch_index,
+                sequence_parallel=module.config.sequence_parallel,
+                wide_input=not module.pre_process,
+            )
+            if not module.pre_process:
+                module.set_input_tensor(hidden)
+            model_parallel_cuda_manual_seed(789 + batch_index)
+            output = ddp(hidden, attention_mask=None)
+            loss = (output.float() - target).square().mean()
+            loss.backward()
+            finalize_model_grads([ddp], pg_collection=pg_collection)
+            torch.cuda.synchronize()
+            replay = module.config.recompute_granularity == "selective"
+            assert read_count - reads_before == (2 if replay else 1)
+            gradients = {}
+            for name, parameter in module.named_parameters():
+                assert parameter.main_grad is not None, name
+                assert torch.isfinite(parameter.main_grad).all(), name
+                gradients[name] = parameter.main_grad
+                if "residual_connection" in name or "shortcut_residual_read" in name:
+                    assert not _is_gtp_parameter(parameter), name
+                    active = parameter.main_grad.flatten()[:_STREAMS]
+                    assert torch.count_nonzero(active) > 0, name
+                if ".mlp.experts." in name:
+                    assert torch.count_nonzero(parameter.main_grad) > 0, name
+
+            records.append(
+                (
+                    output.detach().float().cpu(),
+                    hidden.grad.detach().float().cpu(),
+                    _full_tensors(module, gradients, pg_collection),
+                )
+            )
+    finally:
+        write_handle.remove()
+        read_handle.remove()
+    assert write_dtypes
+    expected_dtype = torch.float32 if module.config.fp32_residual_connection else torch.bfloat16
+    assert all(dtype == expected_dtype for dtype in write_dtypes)
+    return records
+
+
+def _assert_parity(actual, expected, *, gtp=False):
+    for batch_index, (actual_batch, expected_batch) in enumerate(
+        zip(actual, expected, strict=True)
+    ):
+        for kind, actual_value, expected_value in zip(
+            ("output", "input gradient", "main_grad"), actual_batch, expected_batch, strict=True
+        ):
+            if isinstance(actual_value, dict):
+                assert actual_value.keys() == expected_value.keys()
+                pairs = actual_value.items()
+            else:
+                pairs = [(kind, actual_value)]
+                expected_value = {kind: expected_value}
+            for name, value in pairs:
+                if gtp:
+                    # BF16 GTP reductions change cancellation near zero. Bound the error
+                    # relative to each tensor's peak AND norm, not each individual element.
+                    reference = expected_value[name]
+                    atol, rtol = 0.02 * reference.abs().max().item() + 1e-10, 0.0
+                    reference_norm = reference.norm().item()
+                    error_norm = (value - reference).norm().item()
+                    assert error_norm <= 0.02 * reference_norm + 1e-10, (
+                        f"batch {batch_index}, {kind}, {name}: error {error_norm} exceeds "
+                        f"2% of reference norm {reference_norm}"
+                    )
+                else:
+                    atol, rtol = 1e-6, 1e-5
+                torch.testing.assert_close(
+                    value,
+                    expected_value[name],
+                    atol=atol,
+                    rtol=rtol,
+                    msg=lambda detail, name=name: f"batch {batch_index}, {kind}, {name}: {detail}",
+                )

+def _run_wide_shortcut_gtp_parity(compute_symbol):
+    """Shared worker collected by the four-GPU GTP test bucket."""
+
+    if _WORLD_SIZE != 4:
+        pytest.skip("Run with torchrun --nproc-per-node=4")
+    from megatron.core.tensor_parallel.generalized_tensor_parallelism import reset_gtp_state
+
+    saved = reference = gtp_reference = expert_rank = None
+    try:
+        for gtp_size, overlap, replay in (
+            (1, False, False),
+            (2, False, False),
+            (2, True, False),
+            (2, False, True),
+            (2, True, True),
+        ):
+            reset_gtp_state()
+            Utils.initialize_model_parallel(
+                expert_model_parallel_size=2,
+                expert_tensor_parallel_size=1,
+                gtp_remat_size=gtp_size,
+                expert_gtp_remat_size=gtp_size,
+            )
+            pg_collection = ProcessGroupCollection.use_mpu_process_groups()
+            if expert_rank is None:
+                expert_rank = pg_collection.ep.rank()
+            assert pg_collection.ep.rank() == expert_rank
+            model_parallel_cuda_manual_seed(123)
+            torch.manual_seed(123 + pg_collection.ep.rank())
+            module = _build_stack(
+                pg_collection,
+                compute_symbol=compute_symbol,
+                fp32_residual=True,
+                overlap=overlap,
+                replay=replay,
+                tp_size=1,
+                cp_size=1,
+                gtp_size=gtp_size,
+                # Identical initial streams make pre-norm read gradients nearly zero.
+                # Independent wide inputs exercise well-conditioned controller gradients.
+                wide_input=True,
+            )
+            if saved is None:
+                _synchronize_weights(module, pg_collection)
+                saved = _full_tensors(module, dict(module.named_parameters()), pg_collection)
+            _load_weights(module, saved, pg_collection)
+            if gtp_size > 1:
+                sharded = [
+                    parameter for parameter in module.parameters() if _is_gtp_parameter(parameter)
+                ]
+                assert any(getattr(parameter, "allreduce", True) for parameter in sharded)
+                assert any(not getattr(parameter, "allreduce", True) for parameter in sharded)
+            actual = _run_forward_backward(module, pg_collection)
+            if reference is None:
+                reference = actual
+            else:
+                _assert_parity(actual, reference, gtp=True)
+                if gtp_reference is None:
+                    gtp_reference = actual
+                else:
+                    _assert_parity(actual, gtp_reference)
+            del module
+            torch.cuda.synchronize()
+            Utils.destroy_model_parallel()
+    finally:
+        reset_gtp_state()
+        Utils.destroy_model_parallel()
